newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Ex-Haitian police chief gets lawyer in drug case.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Haitian police chief gets lawyer in drug case.

text.p: A controversial Honduran defence lawyer on Wednesday assumed the defence of an exiled Haitian strongman wanted in the United States on drug-trafficking charges.
Lawyer Francisco Lagos predicted he would prevent the extradition of his client, Col. Joseph Michel Francois, to the United States.

Francois was a key part of the 1991-94 military government that seized power in Haiti from elected president Jean-Bertrand Aristide, nearly provoking a hostile U.S. invasion of the Caribbean nation in 1994.
"This case is strictly political," Lagos told reporters. "He (Francois) is innocent of the charges against him, he is being persecuted by U.S. authorities and we are going to avoid extradition."
The flamboyant Lagos is best-known in Honduras for taking up the defence of army officers accused of "disappearing" leftist activists in the 1980s.
"I am going to resolve this case before the court of public opinion," Lagos said. "The (Honduran) government should not go soft before the interests of the (U.S.) State Department."
U.S. defence lawyer Frank Rubino, who also defended former Panamanian strongman Manuel Noriega, is representing Francois in the United States.

At the request of U.S. officials, Honduran police arrested Francois last Friday in the northern city of San Pedro Sula, where he had been living in exile. He is wanted in a Miami court on a series of drug-trafficking charges.

Francois made his first appearance in a Honduran court on Tuesday, when Judge Marco Alvarado announced that a decision on whether to extradite Francois would be made within 60 days of his arrest on March 7.
"He (Francois) has been informed of the charges against him and the rights he has and now he should present evidence against the charges," Alvarado said.
Alvarado determined that Francois had political asylum in Honduras based on an asylum request he made at the Honduran embassy in the Dominican Republic.
However, Interior Minister Efrain Moncada told reporters on Wednesday that Francois was in the country on a tourist visa.
"Michel Francois does not have political asylym," Moncada said.
Legal experts said Francois would be much easier to extradite if he were here only as a tourist.
Francois, currently held in Tegucigalpa's Central Penitentiary, has lived in Honduras since April 1996 along with the former mayor of Port-au-Prince, Frank Rommaind.
